intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-42B (DEE42B) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CACNA1A gene (601011) on chromosome 19p13.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-42B (DEE42B) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CACNA1A gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Compound heterozygous mutations in the CACNA1A gene presumably cause early onset epileptic encephalopathy, and progressive cerebral, cerebellar and optic nerve atrophy with reduced lifespan.
checks.explanation: Paper reports only compound heterozygous mutations; homozygous mutations not addressed.

checks.claim: The CACNA1A gene is located on chromosome 19p13.
checks.evidence_quote: The CACNA1A gene encodes the transmembrane pore-forming alpha-1A subunit of the Cav 2.1 P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channel.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the gene.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-42B (DEE42B) is a severe autosomal recessive neurologic disorder. Seizures begin in early infancy and are hard to treat. Affected children have profound global developmental delay, hypotonia, and poor or absent visual contact. Brain imaging has shown progressive cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, and optic atrophy has been reported. The disorder is the biallelic, usually loss-of-function, counterpart of the CACNA1A-related disorders caused by heterozygous mutation, including DEE42 (DEE42A), episodic ataxia type 2, familial hemiplegic migraine, and spinocerebellar ataxia type 6.

checks.claim: DEE42B is a severe autosomal recessive neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: CACNA1 therefore belongs to the growing list of genes with co-dominantly or both autosomal dominantly and autosomal recessively inherited diseases.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a severe, fatal DEE caused by biallelic variants, i.e. recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: In DEE42B, seizures begin in early infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: Both patients were normal at birth, but developed daily recurrent seizures in early infancy
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: In DEE42B, seizures are hard to treat.
checks.evidence_quote: treatment‐refractory seizures with onset during first 6 months of life
checks.explanation: The paper describes the seizures as refractory to treatment.

checks.claim: Children with DEE42B have profound global developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: At the age of 5, both patients were blind and bedridden with a profound developmental delay.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Children with DEE42B have hypotonia.
checks.evidence_quote: concomitant extreme muscular hypotonia, hypokinesia, and global developmental delay
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Children with DEE42B have poor or absent visual contact.
checks.evidence_quote: She smiled and made laughing noises, but did not make direct visual contact.
checks.explanation: The paper also lists cerebral visual impairment as a consistent feature.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in DEE42B has shown progressive cerebral atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: The brain MRI images showed progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in DEE42B has shown progressive cerebellar atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: The brain MRI images showed progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Optic atrophy has been reported in DEE42B.
checks.evidence_quote: The brain MRI images showed progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: DEE42B is caused by biallelic CACNA1A mutations that are usually loss-of-function.
checks.evidence_quote: further delineates the phenotype associated with bi-allelic CACNA1 variants resulting in complete loss of function.
checks.explanation: Both variants in this family are frameshifts. The paper's table lists most earlier biallelic cases as truncating, with one in-frame case.

checks.claim: DEE42B is the biallelic counterpart of CACNA1A-related disorders caused by heterozygous mutation, including DEE42 (DEE42A), episodic ataxia type 2, familial hemiplegic migraine, and spinocerebellar ataxia type 6.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal-dominant, neurological disorders such as episodic ataxia type 2 (MIM# 108500), spinocerebellar ataxia type 6 (MIM#183086), familial hemiplegic migraine with or without progressive cerebellar ataxia (MIM#141500), and a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (MIM#617106).
checks.explanation: All four heterozygous CACNA1A disorders are listed, and the paper contrasts them with biallelic disease.

paragraphs.text: The autosomal dominant form of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by heterozygous, usually de novo, CACNA1A mutation is designated DEE42A. The autosomal recessive form caused by biallelic CACNA1A mutation is designated DEE42B.

checks.claim: The autosomal dominant form of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by heterozygous CACNA1A mutation is designated DEE42A.
checks.evidence_quote: This phenotype has been classified as developmental and epileptic encephalopathy type 42 (DEE 42; OMIM #617106).
checks.explanation: The paper calls the heterozygous form DEE42, not DEE42A.

checks.claim: The heterozygous CACNA1A mutations causing DEE42A are usually de novo.
checks.evidence_quote: targeted sequencing identified six infants with CACNA1A pathogenic variants (including an affected sibling), which were de novo in 3/5 families.
checks.explanation: The only evidence is de novo variants in 3 of 5 families from one cited study. The paper does not say the variants are usually de novo.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by biallelic CACNA1A mutation is designated DEE42B.
checks.evidence_quote: CACNA1 therefore belongs to the growing list of genes with co-dominantly or both autosomal dominantly and autosomal recessively inherited diseases.
checks.explanation: The paper describes recessive DEE from biallelic variants. It does not use the designation DEE42B.

paragraphs.text: Reinson et al. (2016) reported sibs with early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, severe developmental delay, and progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy. They died in childhood. Their heterozygous carrier relatives had milder CACNA1A-related neurologic features consistent with episodic ataxia.

checks.claim: Reinson et al. (2016) reported sibs with early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe two patients, sister and brother, with compound heterozygous mutations in CACNA1A.
checks.explanation: The sibs had early onset epileptic encephalopathy (title).

checks.claim: The sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) had severe developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: At the age of 5, both patients were blind and bedridden with a profound developmental delay.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) had progressive cerebral atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: The brain MRI images showed progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) had progressive cerebellar atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: The brain MRI images showed progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) had progressive optic nerve atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: The brain MRI images showed progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) died in childhood.
checks.explanation: Only the elder sister is reported to have died: 'The elder sister died at that age.' The brother's death is not reported.

checks.claim: Heterozygous CACNA1A carrier relatives of the sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) had milder CACNA1A-related neurologic features consistent with episodic ataxia.
checks.explanation: The paper says: 'Both of them have intellectual disability and in addition the mother has adult onset cerebellar ataxia with a slowly progressive cerebellar atrophy.' These are intellectual disability and progressive cerebellar ataxia, not episodic ataxia.

paragraphs.text: DEE42B shows autosomal recessive inheritance. Affected individuals carry biallelic CACNA1A mutations. Heterozygous carrier parents can show milder dominant CACNA1A-related phenotypes, such as episodic ataxia.

checks.claim: DEE42B shows autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: This case illustrates the potential for a recessive diagnosis in an apparently sporadic disorder
checks.explanation: The paper describes recessive (biallelic) inheritance.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with DEE42B carry biallelic CACNA1A mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing detected biallelic mutations in CACNA1A
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Heterozygous CACNA1A carrier parents of DEE42B patients can show milder dominant CACNA1A-related phenotypes, such as episodic ataxia.
checks.evidence_quote: Four children with these biallelic variants presented with DEE, leading to death by 6 months of age, whilst both carrier parents had symptoms consistent with EA2
checks.explanation: Carrier parents in a previously reported family had EA2.

paragraphs.text: In affected sibs with early-onset epileptic encephalopathy and progressive brain atrophy, Reinson et al. (2016) used exome sequencing to identify biallelic truncating mutations in the CACNA1A gene. Each parent carried one mutation and had a milder phenotype.

checks.claim: Reinson et al. (2016) studied affected sibs with early-onset epileptic encephalopathy and progressive brain atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: The brain MRI images showed progressive cerebral, cerebellar, and optic nerve atrophy.
checks.explanation: The sibs had early onset epileptic encephalopathy with progressive atrophy.

checks.claim: Reinson et al. (2016) used exome sequencing to identify biallelic truncating CACNA1A mutations in sibs with early-onset epileptic encephalopathy and progressive brain atrophy.
checks.explanation: Not both mutations are truncating. The paper says: 'A missense mutation c.4315T>A (p.Trp1439Arg) in exon 27, and a seven base pair deletion c.472_478delGCCTTCC (p.Ala158Thrfs*6)'.

checks.claim: Each parent of the affected sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) carried one of the CACNA1A mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Their parents and two siblings were heterozygotes for one of those pathogenic mutations and expressed a milder phenotype.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Each carrier parent of the affected sibs reported by Reinson et al. (2016) had a milder phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Their parents and two siblings were heterozygotes for one of those pathogenic mutations and expressed a milder phenotype.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.
